title: The layer that renders a dialog owns its open state
context: Dialog holders disagreed about open state. The set-options panel was already controlled; the lineup panel and ActionButton were uncontrolled, keeping open inside Radix; EditDialogContainer took a third path, fixing <Dialog open> to true and closing by leaving the route. An uncontrolled dialog leaves no seam for the timing of its close: DialogClose closes the moment it is clicked, and the caller can neither read nor veto it. A route holder can also leave in two directions, back to the origin or forward to the result, and parallel routes keep the @modal slot's last content on a soft navigation to a URL the slot has no route for, so leaving forward does not close the modal by itself.
decision: Every dialog that carries an action is controlled: open state lives in the layer that renders the Dialog, and a component inside the overlay never closes itself; it reports success. A holder takes one of two forms: a component holding useState (ActionButton, the set-options panel, the lineup panel), or a route (EditDialogContainer, which closes by leaving the route). A route holder leaves back to the origin with router.back() or forward to the result with router.replace(), and @modal/team/[...catchAll] returns null so that forward navigation closes the modal too. The contract is the same for both forms: the child reports, the holder decides. Only where the dialog and the full page land in the same place does the child navigate to the result itself; the dialog then disappears as a structural consequence of the URL changing. LiberoReplaceDialog has two holders, and each holds its own open state under the same rule.

alternatives.option: Stay uncontrolled and let the child click a hidden DialogClose through a ref
alternatives.reason: No holder changes, but the set-options panel needs that state anyway, and the other two gain a ref hack that bypasses Radix's own interface. Controlled open state is Radix's existing answer to this problem.
One translation fewer, but the child is then welded to a dialog, and a route holder has no setOpen to pass. A reporting interface serves both kinds of holder.

alternatives.option: Make EditDialogContainer hold useState as well
alternatives.reason: Its close already means leaving the route: an @modal intercepting dialog disappearing is the URL changing. Component state would decouple the browser's back button from the dialog. Route ownership is correct there, not an oversight.

alternatives.option: Route holders only ever go back, returning to the origin after every action
alternatives.reason: No catch-all needed, but after adding a player the user lands on the team page and has to find the new player in the list, and an action that must leave the current page, such as removing a member, has nowhere to go. The result page is the natural landing place for a completed action.

alternatives.option: Place the catch-all at the @modal slot root, as the Next.js documentation's example does
alternatives.reason: Widest coverage, but the (tabs) layout would start matching /game, /auth and unknown URLs. Every @modal intercepting route lives under (...)team, so a catch-all under team/ already covers every navigation that needs to close a modal.

consequences: Controlled open state buys a veto, not the ability to close: Radix stores no open value, so Esc, the overlay and DialogClose are each only a request through onOpenChange(false) that the holder may ignore.
EditDialogContainer already had the veto's shape: onOpenChange reaches handleClose, which asks to discard a dirty form instead of closing.
Children converge on one interface: report only on success. A useState holder then calls setOpen(false); a route holder calls router.back() to return or router.replace() to go forward to the result.
Forward navigation after a completed form always replaces, so the saved form does not stay in history for the back button to reopen.
Navigations that already went forward out of a modal, returning to the team page after removing a member and opening a newly created team, are covered by the catch-all as well.
The expand button replaces the dialog's history entry with its full page (window.location.replace), so going back from the full page returns to where the dialog was opened.
The lineup panel's direct import of Dialog from @radix-ui/react-dialog went back through @/components/ui/dialog.
revisitTriggers: Radix provides an official way for DialogClose to wait for an async handler.
A third kind of open-state holder appears that is neither component state nor a route.
An @modal intercepting route appears outside /team; the catch-all has to widen with it.
